title: Tickner Backs New Zealand to Bounce Back Against India in Wellington ODI
excerpt: Bowled out for 185 in Auckland, New Zealand must level the series on Saturday without Devon Conway. Blair Tickner, their No. 11 top-scorer in the opener, says the side moves on fast.
body:
• New Zealand fast bowler Blair Tickner says the hosts will bounce back in the second ODI against India in Wellington on Saturday, November 7, after being bowled out for 185 in the Auckland opener.
  • India lead the series 1-0 after a five-wicket DLS win, chasing a revised 143; Virat Kohli made 74 off 51 balls.
  • Tickner top-scored late for New Zealand with 34 off 23 balls from No. 11, including four sixes.
  • New Zealand will be without opener Devon Conway, ruled out of the rest of the series with concussion; Nick Kelly replaces him.

New Zealand pacer Blair Tickner is confident of a strong response from his side in the second ODI against India, saying the hosts are keen to put a disappointing batting performance in the series opener behind them. India took a 1-0 lead with a five-wicket victory in Auckland on Wednesday, where New Zealand were bowled out for 185. The teams meet again in Wellington on Saturday, November 7.

"Obviously we'd love to score more runs and put a little bit more pressure on them, but I think we move on pretty fast. We know we're a good side, so we're looking forward to obviously scoring more runs and hopefully getting the win in Wellington."

— Blair Tickner, New Zealand fast bowler

What went wrong in Auckland

New Zealand's 185 owed more to their tail than their top order. Tickner, batting at No. 11, made 34 off 23 deliveries, including four sixes and a four, lifting the total late on. Rain then cut India's chase to a revised target of 143, which India reached comfortably, with Virat Kohli making 74 off 51 balls, according to ANI's report via Devdiscourse.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2118151948948140297

Conway out, and a different Wellington pitch

New Zealand's task got harder before the match: opener Devon Conway has been ruled out of the rest of the ODI series with concussion, and Nick Kelly will replace him for the Wellington game. Tickner called the injury "a freak accident" and said Conway was in good spirits, ANI reported.

Tickner is hoping the Wellington surface helps his side more than Eden Park did. "We saw last year against England as well, it was a little bit in the wicket especially here," he said, in comments reported by Khelja. "I don't want to be at a game that's a 400 chase. So I'm looking forward to a little bit of extra bounce, hopefully a bit of nip off the wicket." He also noted Wellington's dimensions differ sharply from Auckland's: the square boundaries are shorter, while the straight boundaries are long. On Kohli, he added that New Zealand still back their skills to get him out. The match starts at 7:30 a.m. IST.
